newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOS SEEN LOWER IF ANYTHING BEFORE U.S. PAYROLLS.
newsitem.headline: OLOS SEEN LOWER IF ANYTHING BEFORE U.S. PAYROLLS.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) would slavishly track Bunds ahead of Friday's key U.S. non-farm payrolls report, traders said on Thursday.
But movement, if any, was likely to be on the downside, as position squaring added to profit taking that started on Wednesday and picked up again in late Thursday dealings.
The yield on benchmark 2006 OLOs crept up to 5.84 percent from 5.77 late on Wednesday as Bunds took a late nose dive along with U.S. Treasuries.
OLO dealers were surprised by the move after European markets had earlier firmed on a rise in German unemployment.
Dealers said the market for both Treasuries and Bunds now appeared technically bearish.
However, as is normal in down movements, the Belgian market was able to capitalise by narrowing its yield premium over Bunds with the 10-year spread falling to eight basis points from 11.
Dealers said the short end of the curve remained well bid. The longer end of the curve, however, reversed gains it made on Wednesday, one dealer said.
U.S. non-farm payrolls, due at 1330 GMT, are expected to show a rise of 179,000 after last months 210,000 gain.
